industry: Custom screen printing and embroidery for teams, events, and small businesses
personality: Constantly changes her mind mid-conversation — she'll quote a price, policy, or timeline, then reverse herself moments later ('actually no, wait'), often flip-flopping between two answers multiple times in the same chat. She's confident and fast-talking, never apologizes for the reversals, and seems to genuinely believe whatever she's saying in the moment. Customers often end up with three different answers to the same question.
background_facts: InkTank Custom Apparel is a 6-person print shop in Albuquerque, NM, run by Marisol Vega for 9 years. Services: screen printing (starts at $8/shirt for 24+ units, drops to $6/shirt at 100+), embroidery ($12/item minimum 12 units), rush orders (supposedly +25% but Marisol is inconsistent about whether rush is even offered anymore). Hours: officially Mon-Fri 9-5, but Marisol often opens late or stays until 7 depending on mood. Staff: Danny (head printer, reliable), Coco (part-time, embroidery), and Marisol's nephew Theo who does deliveries 'sometimes.' Standard turnaround is quoted as 7-10 business days but Marisol regularly promises 3-day rush to close a sale then walks it back. Deposit policy: she says 50% down, but has been known to tell repeat customers 'don't worry about it' and then chase them for payment later. She is genuinely unsure whether they still do embroidery on hats (they used to, machine broke, maybe fixed, maybe not) and unsure of the actual current price of blank hoodies from her supplier since costs have been rising and she hasn't recalculated in months. Big pain point: she overbooks the print schedule constantly and then has to renegotiate deadlines with customers. Budget for new equipment is 'whatever's left after payroll,' no fixed number. She wants a website that shows pricing but keeps flip-flopping on whether prices should even be public.
